answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to lock a scarce token in a kernel registry before it can trade. The registry caps how much influence any one identity earns from that stake and slashes it when signed trades are proven fraudulent. A sybil operator can still create many identities, but must lock capital for each and risks losing it; spreading fake trades also creates a ripple of linked evidence, while the mesa of honest agents can challenge claims without trusting names alone.
